The project provided for the acquisition of vital equipment for scale and field testing to further research objectives, education and outreach. The Center for Wind Energy brings together university, civic and industry partners to create and test new technologies to realize the potential of wind to support the energy needs of the nation. The Center conducts fundamental and applied research primarily in high‐fidelity simulation of wind power systems and components, measurement and analysis of wind fields for diagnostics and model validation, wind tunnel testing, control system design for wind turbines and wind farms, large rotor design, grid integration and energy storage. The Center for Wind Energy provides solutions to the wind power industry and work on novel turbine and system‐level designs. This project provided essential resources to renovate and equip space adjacent to the campus’ state‐of‐the‐art wind tunnel to create laboratory and critical office space for modeling, measurements and control of wind energy systems. The creation of the Intelligent Energy Systems Lab provides an area for students and faculty to design, build and test intelligent systems for wind turbines and wind farms, which enhances the learning experiences and capabilities. The proximity of this new group of students with the fluid mechanics faculty and students located on the second floor of the same building enhances collaboration at the intersection of fluid mechanics, aeromechanics and intelligent systems. As an added benefit, the adjacency to the wind tunnel located in the same building allows easier transportation of experiments constructed in the lab for testing in the tunnel. The lab supports the development of mechatronics and electronics subsystems for research and education in wind turbines and wind farms. This capability is synergistic with other facilities in the building, which currently support fluid mechanics aspects of wind energy research and education such as the BLAST wind tunnel. Wind turbine technology is progressively incorporating more and more electronics and intelligence in a way that resembles the evolution of the aerospace industry in the late 20th century and the automotive industry in the early 21st century. A dedicated lab to these modern technologies is necessary to grow our research and educational programs in wind energy. The renovated facility houses a modern conference room with appropriate A/V capability. The conference room is used to support the recruiting efforts of new members to WindSTAR, a National Science Foundation (NSF) supported Industry/University Collaborative Research Center at UTD, with both in‐person and virtual meetings using modern technology (e.g., monitor, camera, mic, speakers). The conference room also supports participation in formal meetings with the European Academy of Wind Energy, North American Wind Energy Academy and similar events. The Center for Wind Energy at UT Dallas, in partnership with Sandia National Laboratories, is the host of the NAWEA/WindTech 2025 Conference in Dallas and the facilities and equipment procured by this project will be featured to conference participants.
